newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GAC to discuss Albania, Turkey - then off to Rome.
newsitem.headline: GAC to discuss Albania, Turkey - then off to Rome.

text.p: The General Affairs Council on Monday will be an unusual event, with foreign ministers planning an early departure to attend the 40th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome in the Italian capital.
Diplomats said Monday's meeting would be relatively uncontroversial. The agenda includes:
-- BURMA: General System of Preferences (GSP) benefits will be withdrawn from Rangoon on grounds of human rights abuses. It is an "A" point without discussion.
-- SOUTH AFRICA: Ministers will see if Spain is willing to lift its objections to South Africa's fast-track membership of the Lome Convention.
Madrid has blocked the move, seeking an agreement first with South Africa over fishing.
One diplomat said there had been signs that Spain might be willing to move.
-- MEDITERRANEAN: Discussion of status of pending agreements with Egypt, Jordan and Lebanon.
Egypt is the main concern, diplomats said. The lack of movement is considered "embarrassing" ahead of the Euro-Med conference in Malta.
-- TRADE: Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan will address the ministers on the negotiations on a global Information Technology Agreement.

-- FORMER YUGOSLAVIA: Discussion of whether to give Serbia preferential trade treatment. The European Commission has indicated that it will not propose such a move until it is clear that all member states support it.
One diplomat said it was possible that the ministers could ask the Commission for a proposal for the April GAC.
-- ROMANIA: Association Council.
-- ENLARGEMENT: The regular structured dialogue with the countries of central and eastern Europe (CEEC) will take place.

Cyprus will not be included, following the failure at the last GAC to agree a common position. Greece objected to moves supported by the other 14 countries to find a way to involve representatives of the Turkish Cypriot community in the talks.
The ministers will lunch (approximately 1200-1400 GMT) with their CEEC counterparts.
-- TURKEY and CHINA: After the CEEC ministers have left, the ministers will attempt to see whether after last weekend's informal in Apeldoorn, they can now hold an association council with Turkey.
Greece has blocked the council for more than a year over concerns about its dispute with Ankara over the Aegean islands.

EU backing for a U.N. resolution condemning China for human-rights abuses will also be discussed. France held up a decision at the last GAC, seeking a firm commitment of support from the United States.
-- ALBANIA, MIDDLE EAST, GREAT LAKES: Various briefings on the situation in all three regions.
The discussion on Albania will include a report from the EU mission that went to Tirana this week.
